subject.title: fix(gateway): reset channel restart counter after a stable run

question: Should OpenClaw treat a channel run that lasts at least the max restart backoff window as a fresh restart incident, even though that lets stable-but-exiting channels retry indefinitely?
rationale: The code review can verify the bug and the narrow fix shape, but the retry-policy tradeoff changes gateway availability behavior for existing long-running deployments.

options.title: Accept Stable-Run Reset
options.body: Fix the lint issue, add patched real gateway proof, and land the supervisor-window semantics so isolated transport blips do not consume the lifetime crash-loop cap.

options.title: Keep Absolute Cap
options.body: Close or redesign this PR if maintainers want every automatic channel exit to count toward a hard cap regardless of how long the channel stayed healthy.

options.title: Use A Different Window
options.body: Ask for a bounded rolling-window policy if five minutes tied to max backoff is not the desired operational threshold.

recommendation.title: Accept Stable-Run Reset
recommendation.body: Fix the lint issue, add patched real gateway proof, and land the supervisor-window semantics so isolated transport blips do not consume the lifetime crash-loop cap.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame and health-monitor recovery history place steipete closest to this gateway lifecycle policy boundary.
